# Reference

Commands, configuration keys, events, task metadata and result kinds of agentic-team. Every table is generated from the code. For the quickstart see the [README](../README.md); for how the parts work see [Lifecycle](lifecycle.md).

- [`run.py`](#runpy): commands, options, events, exit codes
- [Configuration](#configuration): every key of `.agentic-team.toml`
- [Task metadata](#task-metadata): the `meta` keys of a task and their class on the GitHub backend
- [Results](#results): the result kinds and their statuses

## `run.py`

[scripts/run.py](../scripts/run.py) is the only writer of run state. The Manager runs it from the repository root
through the wrapper:
`"${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/run" [--root DIR] [--tg PATH] [--run-dir DIR] [--json] <command>`.
A `next:` hint that says `run.py <cmd>` means that wrapper with `<cmd>`.
Only `wait` and the host catch-up in `close` sleep or poll, and `wait` writes nothing: `claude --bg` returns at once,
and the Manager runs `record` when a session's message or the end of `wait` wakes it.

### Global options

| Option | Argument | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--root` | `ROOT` | `.` | repository root holding .agentic-team.toml (default: .) |
| `--tg` | `TG` |  | path to tg.py (default: $TASKGRAPH_TG, else scripts/tg-path.sh) |
| `--run-dir` | `RUN_DIR` |  | default: \<root\>/.agentic-team |
| `--json` |  |  | print events as one JSON array |

### Commands

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`launch`](#runpy-launch) | start a worker for a task |
| [`adopt`](#runpy-adopt) | bring a branch started outside run.py under the Manager |
| [`verify`](#runpy-verify) | start a verifier for a PASS result |
| [`record`](#runpy-record) | read the queue and print one line per event |
| [`revise`](#runpy-revise) | after a verifier's verify-failed verdict, send its blocking findings to the same worker session, which fixes them in the same attempt (a revision) |
| [`close`](#runpy-close) | record the verdict and tokens, merge or open a request; done once merged |
| [`round`](#runpy-round) | start a new attempt of a task that waits for its merge, on the same branch and request; --cancel ends it |
| [`merged`](#runpy-merged) | record that a task branch is merged |
| [`repoint`](#runpy-repoint) | pr mode: let a task that waits for its merge follow another request that carries its change |
| [`add`](#runpy-add) | create a task with its dependencies settled: --depends/--blocks or --independent |
| [`stop`](#runpy-stop) | stop a worker for a pause |
| [`abandon`](#runpy-abandon) | abandon a task after attempt 3 failed |
| [`depcheck`](#runpy-depcheck) | record the verdict of the dependency check before a launch as a `check` row |
| [`triage`](#runpy-triage) | record where a Follow-ups line of a result went, as a `triage` row |
| [`status`](#runpy-status) | print the status report |
| [`roles`](#runpy-roles) | list the task roles: the plugin's and the project's, with their defaults; exit 1 when a file is broken |
| [`workflows`](#runpy-workflows) | list the workflows: the plugin's and the project's, with their stages; exit 1 when a file is broken |
| [`stage`](#runpy-stage) | answer the approval of a workflow stage, or split a stage into parts |
| [`check-report`](#runpy-check-report) | check a report file before a session files it; needs no config, Taskgraph or repository |
| [`wait`](#runpy-wait) | poll until something in flight changes, or a time limit; writes nothing |
| [`answer`](#runpy-answer) | answer a worker's ask: the answer is a Taskgraph row, and a doorbell wakes the worker |
| [`steer`](#runpy-steer) | send a running worker a message: change its focus, order or approach inside SCOPE |
| [`inbox`](#runpy-inbox) | show the messages of a task: asks, answers, steers, acks and their delivery state |
| [`notify-queue`](#runpy-notify-queue) | show or clear the operator notices that events queued; it sends nothing |
| [`notify-to`](#runpy-notify-to) | set, clear, or show the session that sessions message after their result |

#### `run.py launch`

```text
run.py launch ID [--keyword KEYWORD] [--tier TIER] [--model MODEL] [--effort EFFORT] [--profile PROFILE] [--attempt ATTEMPT] [--dry-run] [--base BASE] [--cause CAUSE]
```

Renders the brief, creates the task worktree at the base (or continues in it on a retry), starts the worker, and records `session`, `model`, `attempt`, `sessions`, `started_at`, and, on the first launch, `base`. Options: `--keyword`, `--tier`, `--model`, `--effort`, `--profile`, `--attempt`, `--base <sha|branch>`, `--cause <cause>`, `--dry-run`. It records the `plugin` version and the `cause` of the attempt in its `sessions` entry (see `sessions` in [Task metadata](reference.md#task-metadata)). If an open task already has a live session, it records the start instead (`repaired`). It stops a session of the task that is idle with its work filed, or a worker that waits on a prompt after its result (`stopped-idle`), instead of refusing. It refuses a task in a round (`round <id> --cancel` ends it).

| Option | Argument | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ID` |  |  | the task id |
| `--keyword` | `KEYWORD` |  | one or two hyphenated words added to the session name |
| `--tier` | `TIER` |  | a tier or a models.overrides key (overrides the task's tier meta) |
| `--model` | `MODEL` |  | model alias (overrides the tier) |
| `--effort` | `EFFORT` |  | effort level (with --model, or to override the tier's) |
| `--profile` | `PROFILE` |  | Claude profile of the session: a name from [profiles], or default (overrides the tier) |
| `--attempt` | `ATTEMPT` |  | override the next attempt and lift the cap |
| `--dry-run` |  |  | print the brief and the claude command; write nothing |
| `--base` | `BASE` |  | start from this commit or branch instead of the default (a fix on an unmerged branch) |
| `--cause` | `CAUSE` |  | why this attempt starts, recorded in its sessions entry (default: derived from the state of the attempt before it). One of `first`, `review-fix`, `rebase`, `ci-fix`, `retry-issues`, `retry-stopped`, `retry-died`. |

#### `run.py adopt`

```text
run.py adopt ID --branch BRANCH --head HEAD [--pr PR] [--base BASE]
```

Brings a branch started outside `run.py` under the Manager. Options: `--branch`, `--head`, `--pr`, `--base`. It launches nothing.

| Option | Argument | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ID` |  |  | the task id |
| `--branch` | `BRANCH` |  | the local branch that holds the work. Required. |
| `--head` | `HEAD` |  | the branch tip (7 to 40 hex characters). Required. |
| `--pr` | `PR` |  | its open pull or merge request (merge.mode = pr) |
| `--base` | `BASE` |  | the commit the work started from (default: the merge base with the target) |

#### `run.py verify`

```text
run.py verify ID [--ref REF] [--result RESULT] [--model MODEL] [--effort EFFORT] [--profile PROFILE] [--again] [--ci-ref] [--dry-run]
```

Starts a verifier for a `PASS` result, pinned to its `Head`, in the task worktree (read only) or a folder of its own (`[verify] seat`; `seat-fallback` says why it took its own folder). In a revision it resumes the attempt's kept verifier with a revision brief, or starts a new one in the same seat when that verifier is gone. Options: `--ref`, `--result`, `--model`, `--effort`, `--profile`, `--again`, `--ci-ref` (push the worker's `Head` to the scratch branch `ci-<id>-<attempt>` for the verifier to judge its CI runs; pr mode), `--dry-run`. In CI mode (`verify_mode = ci:<name>`) it pushes the branch and finds or starts the CI run instead of a session.

| Option | Argument | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ID` |  |  | the task id |
| `--ref` | `REF` |  | the output under review (default: the result's Head:) |
| `--result` | `RESULT` |  | worker result id (default: the latest for the current attempt) |
| `--model` | `MODEL` |  | model alias (overrides the tier) |
| `--effort` | `EFFORT` |  | effort level (with --model, or to override the tier's) |
| `--profile` | `PROFILE` |  | Claude profile of the verifier: a name from [profiles], or default (overrides the tier) |
| `--again` |  |  | start a new verifier after a verify-blocked verdict or a no-verdict line |
| `--ci-ref` |  |  | push the worker's head to the scratch branch \<[verify] ci_ref_prefix\>\<id\>-\<attempt\> (not the request's branch) so the verifier judges its CI runs; merge.mode = pr |
| `--dry-run` |  |  | print the brief and the claude command; write nothing |

#### `run.py record`

```text
run.py record
```

Reads the queue and prints one line per event: results that arrived, dead, stuck, and stopped sessions, verdicts, merges, open decisions, free slots, and ready tasks. In `pr` mode it also reads the request state, the CI runs, and merges.

#### `run.py revise`

```text
run.py revise ID
```

After a verifier session's `verify-failed` verdict with `blocking:` lines, files a `revise` row, sets `revision`, moves the phase to `running` with no verdict, files one `finding` steer that lists the blocking lines as `F1` to `Fn` and wakes the attempt's own worker session: a revision (see [Revisions](lifecycle.md#revisions-fix-in-place)). Refused when no revision is possible (the message names the old path, `launch` or `abandon`), under a STOP order (exit 3), while the verifier still works, and on a full session cap. Prints `revised`, and `verifier-leftovers` when it stashed the verifier's changes.

| Option | Argument | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ID` |  |  | the task id |

#### `run.py close`

```text
run.py close ID [--verdict VERDICT] [--ref REF] [--ran RAN] [--override-verifier REASON]
```

Records the verdict and tokens, stops the task's live worker and verifier sessions, and merges, pushes and opens a request, or lists the branch as ready to merge. A passing verdict sets `phase=awaiting_merge`, and the task stays in progress until its change is merged; a verdict that does not pass sets `phase=verdict_failed`. Accepts a rebased branch with the same change. Options: `--verdict`, `--ref`, `--ran`, `--override-verifier`. Rerun it on a task that waits for its merge: it resumes at the merge or the push. In `pr` mode it posts the verdict as a comment on the request (`commented`, or `comment-failed`), and it catches up a request that is behind its target (`[merge] catch_up`). A task whose branch holds no commit beyond its base is recorded as merged (`merged_by=no-change`) without a merge, a push or a request. In a round, a PASS with the same change as the verified head and no verifier verdict keeps the round's old verdict (a `Carried:` row).

| Option | Argument | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ID` |  |  | the task id |
| `--verdict` | `VERDICT` |  | the verdict to record, when no verifier gave one (or to override it with --override-verifier). One of `artifact-verified`, `test-verified`, `check-only`, `verify-blocked`, `verify-failed`. |
| `--ref` | `REF` |  | the output the verdict is about (default: the Head: of the worker's result) |
| `--ran` | `RAN` |  | what you ran and saw (stored in your verify result) |
| `--override-verifier` | `REASON` |  | change the verifier's verdict; an upgrade needs a run id or link in --ran |

#### `run.py round`

```text
run.py round ID [KIND] [--cancel] [--keyword KEYWORD] [--tier TIER] [--model MODEL] [--effort EFFORT] [--profile PROFILE] [--attempt ATTEMPT] [--dry-run]
```

Starts a new attempt of a task that waits for its merge, on the same branch and request: kind `rebase`, for a change that conflicts with its target. Options: `--keyword`, `--tier`, `--model`, `--effort`, `--profile`, `--attempt <n>` (also lifts `[rounds] cap`), `--dry-run`. `round <id> --cancel` ends a round: the task waits again at its verified head. Prints `round-started` or `round-cancelled`. See "Round" under [Merging through pull or merge requests](merge.md#merging-through-pull-or-merge-requests).

| Option | Argument | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ID` |  |  | the task id |
| `KIND` | optional |  | what the round is for; its role file has this name. One of `rebase`. |
| `--cancel` |  |  | end the round: the task waits again at its verified head |
| `--keyword` | `KEYWORD` |  | one or two hyphenated words added to the session name |
| `--tier` | `TIER` |  | a tier or a models.overrides key (overrides the role's and the last attempt's) |
| `--model` | `MODEL` |  | model alias (overrides the tier) |
| `--effort` | `EFFORT` |  | effort level (with --model, or to override the tier's) |
| `--profile` | `PROFILE` |  | Claude profile of the session: a name from [profiles], or default (overrides the tier) |
| `--attempt` | `ATTEMPT` |  | the attempt number; it also lifts the [rounds] cap |
| `--dry-run` |  |  | print the brief and the claude command; write nothing |

#### `run.py merged`

```text
run.py merged ID [--by BY]
```

Records that the operator merged a task branch (`--by operator`, the default), marks the task done, then removes its sessions and worktrees.

| Option | Argument | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ID` |  |  | the task id |
| `--by` | `BY` | `operator` | who merged it. One of `operator`, `manager`. |

#### `run.py repoint`

```text
run.py repoint ID --pr PR [--keep-old]
```

`pr` mode: a task that waits for its merge follows request `<n>`, which carries its change (another task's request). Writes `pr`, `pr_branch` and the `repointed_*` keys, unsets `pushed`, sets the merge gate to `<n>`, and closes the task's own request with a comment that names `<n>` (`--keep-old` leaves it open). The phase stays `awaiting_merge`. `record` then only reports `<n>`, and marks the task merged (`merged_by=repoint`, `merged_via=<n>`) once `<n>` is merged; a `target-check` line says, for information, whether the task's commit is in the target. See "Repoint" under [Merging through pull or merge requests](merge.md#merging-through-pull-or-merge-requests).

| Option | Argument | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ID` |  |  | the task id |
| `--pr` | `PR` |  | the number of the request to follow (another task's). Required. |
| `--keep-old` |  |  | leave the task's own request open (default: close it with a comment that names the new one) |

#### `run.py add`

```text
run.py add TITLE [--depends ID [ID ...]] [--blocks ID [ID ...]] [--independent REASON] [--notes NOTES] [--meta KEY=VALUE [KEY=VALUE ...]] [--type TYPE] [--parent PARENT] [--start START] [--due DUE] [--promised PROMISED] [--priority PRIORITY] [--workflow NAME] [--pick A,B] [--seed SEED] [--with STAGE [STAGE ...]] [--skip STAGE [STAGE ...]]
```

Creates a task and settles its dependencies in the same call. It passes `--notes`, `--meta`, `--type`, `--parent`, `--start`, `--due`, `--promised` and `--priority` to `tg add`, and needs exactly one way of settling dependencies: `--depends <ids>` and/or `--blocks <ids>`, or `--independent "<reason>"` (recorded as meta `independent`). Without one it refuses (exit 2). It lists the open and in-progress tasks that may be related, at most 10, strongest first, as `candidate` lines: `SCOPE overlap` (the write paths of `--meta scope=` against each task's; a directory covers the paths under it; write the paths a task must not change after `;` or `；`, or after `不改`, `不要改`, `do not`, `never` or `not:`, and they are not compared; a shared file or a shared directory of four or more segments is strong, a shallower shared directory is marked `shared directory only` and `weak` when it is the only reason), `same #<n> reference` (`#<n>` or `gh issue view <n>` in both notes; an external, decision or milestone shows only for this reason, with its type), and `title words` (two shared words of four letters or more, or three shared Chinese character pairs; the weakest). Order: strong SCOPE overlap, same reference, shallow SCOPE overlap, title. A candidate reachable through the given `--depends`/`--blocks` at any depth reads `linked (via #<id>)`. It prints them when it refuses and when it adds; with `--depends`/`--blocks` each reads `linked` or `not linked`. An `added` line gives the new id and its links. A `--type decision` task needs `--blocks` and prints no candidates. With `--workflow <name>` (needs `[workflow_policy] enabled = true`) it creates a workflow instance in one locked run: the gate runs once for the whole piece of work; the instance task (meta `workflow`, `workflow_record`; `--blocks` ids wait for it) is the parent of one task for each required stage and each `--with <stage>`, created with real `--depends` (a root stage takes the external `--depends`; a later stage depends on each upstream stage and on that stage's approval decision). An optional stage that is not named in `--with` is left out, as is one in `--skip`; the stages after it depend on its upstream stages instead. `--meta scope=` and `verify=` are the instance's: the stages that write code use them, a design stage gets a document path under `[workflow_policy] design_dir`. The notes need a why sentence and `- [ ]` acceptance lines. A stage whose approval is `manager` or `human` also gets a decision under the instance, due once the stage merges (see `stage`). One `workflow-added` line lists the stages, the stages left out and the approvals. `--with` and `--skip` name optional stages only. `--pick "<a>,<b>" --seed <n>` replaces `--workflow`: the two typed answers (a workflow name or `unsure`; the Manager's, then the subagent's from the prompt of seed n+1) resolve to one workflow: the same name wins; two names take the one with fewer required stages; a name beside `unsure` takes the name; two `unsure` take `figure-it-out`; `[workflow_policy] when_unsure` changes the unsure rows. The answers, seeds and rule go into the record, with a `workflow-picked` line. A matching `[[workflow_rule]]` that has `require_stage` forces that stage on (`--with`), or moves the work to the lightest workflow that has it, and refuses `--skip` of it; each match is a `workflow-rule` line and a row of the record. An unsure pick or a rule change queues a `workflow-pick` notice when `notifications.events` lists it, and shows in `status` and the daily digest. See [Workflows](roles-and-briefs.md#workflows).

| Option | Argument | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `TITLE` |  |  | the task title |
| `--depends` | `ID [ID ...]` |  | tasks this one needs first |
| `--blocks` | `ID [ID ...]` |  | tasks that need this one first |
| `--independent` | `REASON` |  | no task is related; recorded as meta independent=\<reason\> |
| `--notes` | `NOTES` |  | the task notes: purpose and acceptance criteria (passed to tg add) |
| `--meta` | `KEY=VALUE [KEY=VALUE ...]` |  | meta pairs for the task, such as scope=, verify= and tier= (passed to tg add) |
| `--type` | `TYPE` |  | passed to tg add --type |
| `--parent` | `PARENT` |  | passed to tg add --parent |
| `--start` | `START` |  | passed to tg add --start |
| `--due` | `DUE` |  | passed to tg add --due |
| `--promised` | `PROMISED` |  | passed to tg add --promised |
| `--priority` | `PRIORITY` |  | passed to tg add --priority |
| `--workflow` | `NAME` |  | create one task for each stage of this workflow, under an instance task (`run.py workflows` lists them); --meta scope= and verify= are the instance's |
| `--pick` | `A,B` |  | choose the workflow from two typed answers, the Manager's and the subagent's ("feature,unsure"); needs --seed; leave out --workflow (`run.py workflows --pick-prompt` makes the prompts) |
| `--seed` | `SEED` |  | with --pick: the seed of the Manager's own prompt; the subagent's prompt used seed+1 |
| `--with` | `STAGE [STAGE ...]` |  | with --workflow: create this optional stage (it is left out otherwise) |
| `--skip` | `STAGE [STAGE ...]` |  | with --workflow: leave this optional stage out, and say so in the record |

#### `run.py stop`

```text
run.py stop ID
```

Stops a worker and files a `STOPPED` result. The row says `Reason: pause` when the standing orders' first line is `STOP`: a pause, which does not use an attempt. Else it says `Reason: recover`: a stop that recovers a quiet or broken session, which counts as an attempt.

| Option | Argument | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ID` |  |  | the task id |

#### `run.py abandon`

```text
run.py abandon ID reason [--why WHY]
```

Marks a task abandoned after attempt 3 failed, and stops the task's live worker and verifier sessions. `<reason>` is a code: `died`, `tool-error`, `stuck`, `failed` (the attempts failed on their merits), `scope-wrong` (the brief, SCOPE or a dependency was wrong), `superseded` (another task or request replaces it) or `operator` (the operator dropped it). `--why` is required: one line of free text, stored in the meta `abandoned_why`, the `ABANDONED` row (`Abandoned:`, `Why:`) and the `abandoned` line. `unknown` is gone; a missing `--why` is refused. It also drops a task that waits for its merge: its branch stays unmerged, and in `pr` mode its request stays open on the host for the operator to close.

| Option | Argument | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ID` |  |  | the task id |
| `reason` |  |  | the reason code: died, tool-error, stuck, failed, scope-wrong, superseded, operator. One of `died`, `tool-error`, `stuck`, `failed`, `scope-wrong`, `superseded`, `operator`. |
| `--why` | `WHY` |  | one line of free text: what happened and why the task is dropped (required) |

#### `run.py depcheck`

```text
run.py depcheck ID --verdict VERDICT --body-file BODY_FILE
```

Records the verdict of the dependency check as a `check` row (status `OK`, `MISSING` or `NOT-CHECKED`) of the attempt that the check is for (the next one): `Check: dependency`, `Verdict:`, then the subagent's answer. The Manager runs it after the `agentic-team:dependency-check` subagent answers, so that a retro can count the checks against the launches. It changes no task state.

| Option | Argument | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ID` |  |  | the task id |
| `--verdict` | `VERDICT` |  | the subagent's verdict: ok, missing (a `missing:` line) or not-checked (a `not checked:` or `ask:` line). One of `ok`, `missing`, `not-checked`. Required. |
| `--body-file` | `BODY_FILE` |  | the subagent's answer. Required. |

#### `run.py triage`

```text
run.py triage ID --row RESULT#LINE --to KIND [ID] [KIND [ID] ...] [--why WHY]
```

Records where a `Follow-ups:` line of one of the task's results went, as a `triage` row (status `TASK`, `ISSUE` or `DISMISSED`) with `Row:`, `Line:` (the line as written), `To:` and `Why:`. `<line>` counts the result's `Follow-ups:` lines from 1. `dismissed` needs `--why`; `task <id>` must be a task of this project. A retro joins the row to the follow-up line. A later row for the same line replaces the earlier one in a retro. It changes no task state.

| Option | Argument | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ID` |  |  | the task id |
| `--row` | `RESULT#LINE` |  | a result id and the number of one of its Follow-ups lines, 3352#2. Required. |
| `--to` | `KIND [ID] [KIND [ID] ...]` |  | `task \<id\>`, `issue \<n\>` or `dismissed`. Required. |
| `--why` | `WHY` |  | the reason (required for dismissed) |

#### `run.py status`

```text
run.py status [--since SINCE] [--limit LIMIT] [--mark] [--brief]
```

Prints the status report as Markdown tables. Options: `--since`, `--limit`, `--mark`. A task that waits for its merge is listed under "Closed, awaiting merge" (`awaiting_merge` in `--json`), not under "In flight"; it is listed as done once merged. It also counts the `Follow-ups:` lines of the worker reports filed in the period by label, with `unlabelled` for a line without a known label (verifier reports, the Manager's `DIED`, `STOPPED`, `ABANDONED` and `BLOCKED` rows, and `leftover ...` lines are not counted), and gives the mean attempts of the tasks done in the period. `--json` has them as `follow_ups` and `attempts` (`{"tasks", "mean"}`). When an in-flight session runs under another Claude profile, the In flight table gains a `Profile` column (`Profile` in `--json`). When a session's token usage is known, the Done and In flight tables gain an `Est. cost` column (see [Cost in status](operations.md#cost-in-status)).

| Option | Argument | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--since` | `SINCE` |  | 7d, 2w, or an ISO date (default: last --mark, else 7d) |
| `--limit` | `LIMIT` | `25` | max rows per table (default 25) |
| `--mark` |  |  | save now as the start of the next report |
| `--brief` |  |  | only the work not yet closed: in flight, waiting, verdict not closed, failed, awaiting merge |

#### `run.py roles`

```text
run.py roles
```

Lists every task role, one line each: the name, its source (`plugin`, `project`, `project, overrides plugin`, or `project, extends plugin:<name>`), what it fits, its tier, verify kind and skills. `--json` prints one object per role. Read only. A broken role file is listed with its error, and the command exits 1, so you see it before a `launch` fails. See [Roles](roles-and-briefs.md#roles).

#### `run.py workflows`

```text
run.py workflows [--check] [--pick-prompt] [--seed SEED] [--title TITLE] [--notes-file FILE] [--scope SCOPE] [--resolve A,B]
```

Lists every workflow, one line each: the name, its source (`plugin`, `project`, `project, overrides plugin`, or `project, extends plugin:<name>`), its description and its stages, in file order, as `prd → ux? → spec → impl* → test` (`?` marks an optional stage, `*` a stage that may be split). `--json` prints one object per workflow, with each stage's resolved role, verify kind, approval, estimate and `after`. Read only. A broken file is listed with its problems, each as `<file>:<line>: <problem>`, and the command exits 1; a problem of `stages.toml` is listed the same way. `--check` prints only the problems, or one `workflows-checked` line; it is the same check that `config.py check` runs when `[workflow_policy] enabled` is true or the project has workflow files. `--pick-prompt` prints the prompt that asks which workflow fits a piece of work (`--title`, `--notes-file`, `--scope`): the task text and the workflows as `A. <name>: <description>`, with `unsure` among them, in an order that `--seed` fixes; the same seed gives the same order. `--resolve "<a>,<b>"` prints which workflow two typed answers resolve to, and records nothing. See [Workflows](roles-and-briefs.md#workflows).

| Option | Argument | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--check` |  |  | print only the problems of the workflow files and the stage library, or ok |
| `--pick-prompt` |  |  | print the prompt that picks a workflow for a piece of work |
| `--seed` | `SEED` |  | with --pick-prompt: the seed that shuffles the options (required) |
| `--title` | `TITLE` |  | with --pick-prompt: the title of the work |
| `--notes-file` | `FILE` |  | with --pick-prompt: a file that holds the notes of the work |
| `--scope` | `SCOPE` |  | with --pick-prompt: the SCOPE paths or areas of the work |
| `--resolve` | `A,B` |  | resolve two typed answers (names or unsure) to one workflow, as `add --pick` does; read only |

#### `run.py stage`

```text
run.py stage ID ACTION [STAGE] [--with STAGE [STAGE ...]] [--skip STAGE [STAGE ...]] [--default] [--by BY] [--note NOTE] [--decline-split REASON] [--part TITLE] [--meta KEY=VALUE [KEY=VALUE ...]] [--depends ID [ID ...]]
```

`approve`: answers the approval decision of a stage of a workflow instance. It refuses while the stage is not merged. A `manager` approval checks workflow facts only: every `decision:` follow-up of the stage is triaged (`triage`), and each splittable stage after it is split (`split`) or declined with `--decline-split "<one line>"`. A `human` approval needs `--by operator`, after the owner has answered. `--default` applies the default (approve) of an approval that is past its due time; it refuses an approval that holds (`on_timeout = "hold"`). `record` applies the same default itself at the due time (`approval-due`), so `--default` is for a Manager that runs it by hand. `split`: adds a part to a stage whose workflow sets `split: true`, before the stage has an attempt. The first call re-titles the stage's own task as part 1; each later call creates a part with the same upstream dependencies, and every later stage then depends on all parts. `--meta scope=` is required. A part whose files overlap a sibling's must name it with `--depends`. `recheck`: matches the `[[workflow_rule]]` tables again against the SCOPE paths of the stages and the `area` (a part added by `split` does it too); a rule that is new to the record gets a `workflow-rule` line, and one whose stage is missing gets the way out. `rechoose <workflow>` (`--by operator`, `--note`, `--with`, `--skip`): the owner's override; it replaces the stages with those of another workflow, with the rules applied again, only while no stage has started. It is recorded under `overrides` and is not an adjustment. See [Workflows](roles-and-briefs.md#workflows).

| Option | Argument | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ID` |  |  | the id of the workflow instance task |
| `ACTION` |  |  | approve: answer the stage's approval decision; split: add a part to a stage that may be split; recheck: match the hard rules again; rechoose: replace the stages with those of another workflow, before any stage has started. One of `approve`, `split`, `recheck`, `rechoose`. |
| `STAGE` | optional |  | the stage id, for example spec or impl (rechoose: the workflow name; recheck: none) |
| `--with` | `STAGE [STAGE ...]` |  | rechoose: create this optional stage |
| `--skip` | `STAGE [STAGE ...]` |  | rechoose: leave this optional stage out |
| `--default` |  |  | approve: apply the default of an approval that is past its due time |
| `--by` | `BY` | `manager` | approve: who answers; a `human` approval needs operator. rechoose: who overrides. One of `manager`, `operator`. |
| `--note` | `NOTE` |  | approve: one line for the decision's notes; rechoose: why |
| `--decline-split` | `REASON` |  | approve: one line on why a splittable stage after this one is not split |
| `--part` | `TITLE` |  | split: the title of the part; the first call names part 1, the stage's own task |
| `--meta` | `KEY=VALUE [KEY=VALUE ...]` |  | split: meta of the part; scope= is required |
| `--depends` | `ID [ID ...]` |  | split: sibling parts that this part waits for; needed when their files overlap |

#### `run.py check-report`

```text
run.py check-report FILE [--mailbox CTX] [--verifier] [--acceptance N] [--require-ran PREFIX] [--check COMMAND] [--check-timeout SECONDS] [--base SHA] [--target REF]
```

Checks a report file before a session files it: a `Status:` line with `PASS`, `ISSUES` or `BLOCKED`, a `Checkpoint:` line, and a label on each `Follow-ups:` line. A leading `- ` or `* ` is ignored; `None` and `leftover ...` lines pass. With `--acceptance <n>`, a `PASS` report also needs at least `<n>` non-empty lines under `Evidence:` (the first may sit on the `Evidence:` line; the lines run to the next field; a `None` line does not count), else the problem is ``PASS needs one `Evidence:` line per ACCEPTANCE line: found <k>, ACCEPTANCE has <n>``; `ISSUES` and `BLOCKED` reports are not counted, and without the option nothing changes. Without `--verifier`, an `ISSUES` or `BLOCKED` report needs an `Asked:` line: ask ids (`Asked: #12, #15`) or `Asked: none: <one-line reason>`, else the problem is ``<STATUS> needs an `Asked:` line: ...``. Prints `ok`, or one `run.py: <problem>` line per problem on stderr and exits 2. It reads only the file, so it needs no config, no Taskgraph and no repository; `--json` does not change its output. The brief's REPORT section names it with the session's report file. A worker's brief adds `--mailbox <context file>`: the command then also reads Taskgraph through that file and names a steer of the worker's attempt that has no ack (if Taskgraph cannot be read, it behaves as without the option) and `--acceptance <n>` with the number of ACCEPTANCE items of the task. The brief adds more for a worker: `--base <sha>` (the task's `base` meta, else the attempt's start) with `--target <ref>` (the fetched remote target branch in `pr` mode, else the branch of the main checkout), and one `--require-ran <prefix>` for each prefix that `[report] require_ran` lists for the task's verify kind. A rebase round gets none of these. With `--base`, a `PASS` report must name under `Files:` every file that `git diff --name-only <start>...HEAD` lists in the worker's worktree, where `<start>` is the newer of `--base` and the merge base of HEAD with `--target`: the task's own commits only, never what a rebase onto the target brought in (a stacked base that is still unmerged is newer than the merge base, so it stays the start; after a restack the merge base is); a deleted file counts as its path and a renamed file as its new path; when more than 20 files changed, a directory entry (`src/`, `src/**`) names the files under it; `ISSUES` and `BLOCKED` reports are not checked, and when git cannot say (an unknown base) nothing is checked. With `--require-ran`, a `PASS` report needs a `Ran:` line that starts with each prefix (a list marker and backticks in front are ignored), else the problem names the missing ones. A verifier's check command has neither: a verifier's report has no `Evidence:` line. With `--verifier`, a report that has more than one `Issues:` field gets the warning "write a single `Issues:` field, one finding per line" (exit code unchanged); every `Issues:` field is read all the same, and a line may be `blocking:` or `blocking[<category>]:` with a category from `stale-ref`, `claim`, `test`, `scope`, `shots`, `behaviour`. `record` does not check the evidence, `Files:` or `Ran:` lines of a report that it recovers from a transcript or a file; it does run the `[report] checks` of a worker `PASS` (see [Report checks](operations.md#report-checks)). With `--check`, the command also refuses a `PASS` while `git status --porcelain` lists changes before or after the checks.

| Option | Argument | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `FILE` |  |  | the report file that the brief's REPORT section names |
| `--mailbox` | `CTX` |  | a worker's context file: also name a steer of its attempt that has no ack (reads Taskgraph through the file's tg.py) |
| `--verifier` |  |  | the report is a verifier's: an ISSUES report needs a `blocking:` label on every Issues line, and a report with only non-blocking findings is a PASS |
| `--acceptance` | `N` |  | a PASS report needs at least N non-empty lines under Evidence:, one for each ACCEPTANCE line of the task |
| `--require-ran` | `PREFIX` |  | a worker PASS report needs a `Ran:` line that starts with PREFIX (repeat it; the brief passes [report] require_ran) |
| `--check` | `COMMAND` |  | a worker PASS report needs this command to exit 0 in the worktree (repeat it; the brief passes [report] checks) |
| `--check-timeout` | `SECONDS` | `600` | the time each --check command may take (default: the [report] check_timeout_seconds default; the brief passes the project's value) |
| `--base` | `SHA` |  | the commit the task's own change starts from: a worker PASS report must name under `Files:` each file that `git diff --name-only \<start\>...HEAD` lists, \<start\> being the newer of SHA and the merge base of HEAD with --target |
| `--target` | `REF` |  | the branch the task merges into (with --base) |

#### `run.py wait`

```text
run.py wait [--timeout TIMEOUT] [--interval INTERVAL] [--tg-interval TG_INTERVAL] [--host-interval HOST_INTERVAL]
```

Polls until something in flight changes and prints one `changed` line per change. It prints `timeout` after `--timeout` seconds (default 1800, at most 6600), or `nothing-in-flight` at once when no session runs and, in `pr` mode, no request is open and no CI run is read. It compares each poll with its own first read: the results of each task in progress, the state of each of their sessions, the open decisions, and in `pr` mode each open request of a closed task and the newest CI run that `record` reads. Options: `--tg-interval` (default 5 seconds, from `[messaging] tg_poll_seconds`: how often Taskgraph is read, so a new ask row wakes the Manager within seconds), `--interval` (default 30 seconds: how often `claude agents` is read), `--host-interval` (default 300 seconds; the host limits its rate). It writes nothing.

| Option | Argument | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--timeout` | `TIMEOUT` | `1800` | seconds to wait at most (default 1800, at most 6600) |
| `--interval` | `INTERVAL` | `30` | seconds between two reads of claude agents (default 30) |
| `--tg-interval` | `TG_INTERVAL` |  | seconds between two reads of Taskgraph (default: [messaging] tg_poll_seconds, 5); claude agents is still read every --interval, so a new ask or answer row wakes the Manager sooner |
| `--host-interval` | `HOST_INTERVAL` | `300` | pr mode: seconds between two reads of the code host (default 300; the host limits its rate, so keep the default) |

#### `run.py answer`

```text
run.py answer ID [--ask ASK] [--file FILE] [--default] [--decision DECISION] [--supersede] [--by BY]
```

Answers a worker's `ask` row with `--file F`, `--default` (the ask's own `Default:` line) or `--decision <id>` (a done decision with `--meta ask=<ask id>`; its notes are the answer). Options: `--ask <row id>` (default: the newest open ask of the current attempt), `--supersede` (answer an ask again), `--by operator`. It refuses an ask of an ended attempt and a second answer without `--supersede`. It files the `answer` row, then delivers the doorbell.

| Option | Argument | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ID` |  |  | the task id |
| `--ask` | `ASK` |  | the ask row id (default: the newest open ask of the current attempt) |
| `--file` | `FILE` |  | the answer text |
| `--default` |  |  | answer with the ask's own Default line |
| `--decision` | `DECISION` |  | a decision that is done and has --meta ask=\<ask id\>: its notes are the answer |
| `--supersede` |  |  | answer an ask that is already answered |
| `--by` | `BY` | `manager` | who sends it, as the row's author. One of `manager`, `operator`. |

#### `run.py steer`

```text
run.py steer ID --file FILE [--kind KIND] [--interrupt] [--by BY]
```

Sends a running worker a steer: `--file F`, `--kind info|redirect|wrap-up` (`finding` is refused: only `revise` files it), `--by operator`, `--interrupt` (stop and resume a busy worker). It refuses a verifier, and a task with no live worker in its current attempt (the message says to write the text in the task notes).

| Option | Argument | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ID` |  |  | the task id |
| `--file` | `FILE` |  | the steer text. Required. |
| `--kind` | `KIND` | `info` | info, redirect or wrap-up; finding is refused here, because only revise files it. One of `info`, `redirect`, `wrap-up`, `finding`. |
| `--interrupt` |  |  | stop the worker and resume it with the doorbell, even when busy |
| `--by` | `BY` | `manager` | who sends it, as the row's author. One of `manager`, `operator`. |

#### `run.py inbox`

```text
run.py inbox ID
```

Shows the task's messages: asks, answers, steers and acks, with the delivery state of each. Read only.

| Option | Argument | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ID` |  |  | the task id |

#### `run.py notify-queue`

```text
run.py notify-queue [--clear] [--add ADD] [--do DO] [--digest] [--sent]
```

Shows the operator notices that events queued, one `notify` line each (`[event] what happened`, then `next:` what the operator can do, and for a decision its default and deadline); `notify-queue: empty` when there are none. `--clear` shows them, then counts them as sent and empties the queue. `--add all-done|blocked "<line>" [--do "<text>"]` queues one the Manager decides. `--digest` prints the daily digest once a day when `notifications.digest = "daily"`, of what happened since the last digest that was marked as sent; `--digest --sent` marks the printed digest as sent. It sends nothing.

| Option | Argument | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--clear` |  |  | show the notices, then count them as sent and empty the queue |
| `--add` | `ADD` |  | queue a notice for an event that has no run.py line: all-done or blocked, with one plain line |
| `--do` | `DO` |  | with --add: what the operator can do |
| `--digest` |  |  | print the daily digest once a day when notifications.digest is daily |
| `--sent` |  |  | with --digest: the digest was sent; count it as made |

#### `run.py notify-to`

```text
run.py notify-to [NAME] [--clear]
```

Stores the Manager's session name in the run directory. Each brief rendered after that tells its session to send one line with SendMessage after its `result add`, to `uds:<the Manager's inbox socket>` when `manager.addr` holds it, else to the name. `--clear` removes the name; with no argument it prints the name.

| Option | Argument | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `NAME` | optional |  | the bare session name from the first line of ListAgents |
| `--clear` |  |  | remove the name; new briefs have no notify step |

### Output and exit codes

Each event is one line: `<event> #<id> attempt <n>: <detail>`, followed by ` | next: <step>` when a step follows.
`--json` prints one array of `{"event", "task", "attempt", "session", "detail", "next"}` objects and nothing else on
stdout (`status --json` prints one object). Refusals go to stderr as `run.py: <message>`. `local` mode never runs `gh`
or `glab`.

`run.py` finds `tg.py` through `--tg`, then `$TASKGRAPH_TG`, then `scripts/tg-path.sh`. How it matches a session to
its task is in [Lifecycle](lifecycle.md#how-runpy-matches-a-session-to-its-task).

| Exit code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | The command ran. An event may still say `died` or `kept`. |
| 1 | A tool failed: `tg`, `git`, or `claude`. |
| 2 | The command refused. The message names the fix. |
| 3 | The standing orders say `STOP`. Only `launch` returns it. |

### Events

`run.py` prints 119 events. A name that is not in `scripts/events.py` is refused.

| Event | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `launched` | A worker started for a task: its model, session, worktree and brief. |
| `dry-run` | A dry run: the brief and the claude command, with nothing written. |
| `repaired` | An open task already had a live session; run.py recorded the start instead of launching again. |
| `stopped-idle` | A session of the task was idle with its work filed (or waited on a prompt after its result); launch stopped it. |
| `adopted` | A branch that was started outside run.py is now under the Manager. |
| `resumed` | A task that was closed earlier continues at its push or merge step. |
| `closed` | The task was closed earlier and is marked done now. |
| `legacy` | A task started under an older version that run.py cannot continue; the next step names the way out. |
| `warn` | A warning that does not stop the command, for example a role file that is too long. |
| `role` | One task role, as `run.py roles` lists it. |
| `role-broken` | A role file with an error, as `run.py roles` lists it; the command exits 1. |
| `workflow` | One workflow, as `run.py workflows` lists it: its source, description and stages. |
| `workflow-broken` | A workflow file or a stage library file with an error, as `run.py workflows` lists it; the command exits 1. |
| `workflows-checked` | `run.py workflows --check` found no problem. |
| `workflow-added` | `add --workflow` created an instance: its stages, the stages left out and the approvals. |
| `workflow-picked` | The two typed answers of a workflow pick, their seeds and the resolution (`add --pick`; `workflows --resolve` records nothing). |
| `workflow-rule` | A hard rule matched an instance: forced a stage on, moved the work to another workflow, or matched again after the SCOPE changed. |
| `workflow-rechosen` | `stage rechoose` replaced the stages of an instance that had not started with those of another workflow. |
| `approval-opened` | A stage merged and its approval decision is open: its due time and default; a `human` one is now the owner's. |
| `approval-due` | An approval decision passed its due time and `record` applied its default (approve). |
| `approved` | A stage approval was answered: by the Manager, the owner or the default. |
| `split` | A stage was split: the new part, or the first part named. |
| `sessions-restored` | The local Taskgraph cache had no `sessions` meta; run.py rebuilt it from `claude agents`. |
| `sessions-lost` | A task in progress has no `sessions` meta and no matching session row; its worker may run on another machine. |
| `verifying` | A verifier started for a PASS result: model, session, ref, verify kind and seat. |
| `seat-fallback` | The verifier took a folder of its own, and the line says why the task worktree was not used. |
| `ci-ref` | The worker's head was pushed to the scratch branch that a CI verify judges. |
| `ci-ref-deleted` | Scratch branches of CI verify were deleted from the remote. |
| `ci-dispatched` | A CI run was started for the pushed head. |
| `ci-waiting` | No CI run exists for the head yet, and the line says why. |
| `ci-pending` | A CI run for the head exists and has not finished. |
| `verified` | A verdict arrived for the task: the level and who gave it. |
| `no-verdict` | A verifier ended with no result and no report. |
| `verifier-leftovers` | The verifier left changes in the task worktree; run.py stashed them. |
| `unclosed` | A verdict exists and the task is not closed; the next step names the command. |
| `override` | The Manager changed a verifier's verdict with `close --override-verifier`. |
| `verdict` | `close` recorded a verdict that does not close the task. |
| `revised` | A revision started: the blocking findings went to the attempt's own worker session. |
| `arrived` | A worker result arrived for the attempt. |
| `running` | A worker session is busy on the attempt. |
| `unknown` | A session has a status that run.py cannot read; it was not filed as DIED. |
| `died` | A session ended with no result; run.py filed DIED. |
| `stuck` | A session waits on a permission prompt; run.py filed BLOCKED. |
| `gated` | The task waits for a decision that blocks it. |
| `salvaged` | run.py recovered a report from a transcript or a file and filed it. |
| `stopping` | A session that run.py stopped has not exited yet. |
| `stopped` | A worker was stopped (`stop`, a recovery or a close) and a STOPPED result filed, or nothing was left to commit. |
| `kept-session-stopped` | A worker or verifier that waited for a revision was stopped after `keep_sessions_minutes`. |
| `revision-gap` | The task is in a revision that this machine has no `revise` row for; record takes no action on it. |
| `locked` | Another run.py holds the task's lock; record skips the task this time. |
| `checks-skipped` | The `[report] checks` of a worker PASS did not run, and the line says why. |
| `checks-failed` | The `[report] checks` failed at the head of a PASS; run.py filed ISSUES. |
| `phase-mismatch` | The stored phase and the task's fields disagree; record leaves the task until the meta is fixed. |
| `transition-error` | An event has no row in the phase transition table for the task's phase; record goes on and exits 1. |
| `host-error` | The code host failed for this task; record goes on with the others and exits 1. |
| `tokens` | The tokens of the attempt's sessions, summed from the transcripts, or why none were found. |
| `unmanaged` | Tasks in progress that run.py did not start. |
| `decision` | An open decision task: its title, decider, due date and what it blocks. |
| `slots` | Live sessions against `sessions.max_parallel`. |
| `waits` | A ready task waits for a dependency that is not merged. |
| `ready` | The tasks that are ready to launch. |
| `candidate` | A task that may be related to the one `add` creates or refuses. |
| `added` | `add` created a task and settled its dependencies. |
| `depchecked` | The verdict of the dependency check was recorded. |
| `triaged` | The destination of a Follow-ups line was recorded. |
| `nothing-in-flight` | `wait` found no live session, open request or CI run to watch. |
| `changed` | Something in flight changed during `wait`. |
| `timeout` | `wait` ended with no change after the time limit. |
| `asked` | A worker asked the Manager a question. |
| `asking` | A worker waits for an answer to an ask. |
| `ask-due` | An ask has had no answer for `messaging.ask_due_minutes`. |
| `answered` | `answer` filed an answer row and delivered the doorbell. |
| `answer-seen` | The worker acknowledged an answer. |
| `steered` | `steer` filed a steer row and delivered the doorbell. |
| `steer-seen` | The worker acknowledged a steer. |
| `steer-pending` | A steer was delivered several times and never acknowledged. |
| `deliver-fallback` | The doorbell could not reach the session; record ends the attempt. |
| `deliver-copy` | A resume started a copy of the session; run.py stopped the original. |
| `inbox` | `inbox` found no messages for the task. |
| `message` | One message of a task, as `inbox` shows it. |
| `notify-to` | The Manager's session name for the notify step of briefs: set, cleared or shown. |
| `notify-queue` | The result of queueing or showing the operator notices. |
| `notify-digest` | The daily digest was skipped, or the reason it was not made. |
| `notify` | One queued operator notice. |
| `kept` | A branch or worktree folder stays after a merge, and the line says why. |
| `removed` | A merged task's worktree folder was removed. |
| `merged` | The task's change is merged and the task is done. |
| `unmerged` | A closed branch is ready to merge in local mode. |
| `unpublished` | A task was closed and its branch is not pushed yet. |
| `conflict` | The change conflicts with its target (or a post-rebase check failed); the next step names the decision or round. |
| `no-change` | The branch holds no commit beyond its base; the task is recorded as merged with nothing to merge. |
| `published` | A pull or merge request was opened for the task. |
| `pushed` | The task branch was pushed to the remote. |
| `push-failed` | A push did not reach the remote. |
| `push-refused` | The remote branch is gone or the push was refused. |
| `commented` | The verdict was posted as a comment on the request. |
| `comment-failed` | Posting the verdict comment failed. |
| `rebased` | A stacked branch was rebased onto its target after its base merged under other SHAs. |
| `catch-up-local` | The host cannot rebase the request; run.py rebases it in the task worktree. |
| `pr-rebased` | The request's head is a rebase of the pushed head (by the host or by someone else). |
| `pr-pending` | The host says the request is up to date with its target; waiting. |
| `pr-behind` | The request is behind its target and the host did not rebase it. |
| `pr-unpinned` | The request is open and no pushed head is recorded, so nothing merges. |
| `pr-closed` | The request was closed without a merge. |
| `pr-changed` | The request's head is not the pushed head; run.py does not merge it. |
| `pr-draft` | The request is a draft. |
| `pr-blocked` | The host reports the request blocked (checks, reviews or protection). |
| `pr-retargeted` | A followed request merged into a different branch than the task's target. |
| `ready-to-merge` | The request is clean and waits for a MERGE: line or the end of a pause. |
| `merge-failed` | The host refused the merge. |
| `follows` | A task follows another task's open request. |
| `repointed` | A task now follows another request that carries its change. |
| `target-check` | Whether the task's commit is in the target, for information. |
| `kept-open` | The task's own request stays open after a repoint. |
| `superseded` | The task's own request was closed with a comment that names the request it follows. |
| `round-started` | A round started: a new attempt on the same branch and request. |
| `round-cancelled` | A round ended; the task waits again at its verified head. |
| `round-not-needed` | A round that runs is no longer needed, and the line says why. |
| `abandoned` | A task was abandoned: the reason code and the words. |

### Fixed values

| Name | Values |
|---|---|
| Verdict levels (`close --verdict`) | `artifact-verified`, `test-verified`, `check-only`, `verify-blocked`, `verify-failed` |
| Launch causes (`launch --cause`) | `first`, `review-fix`, `rebase`, `ci-fix`, `retry-issues`, `retry-stopped`, `retry-died` |
| Abandon reasons | `died`, `tool-error`, `stuck`, `failed`, `scope-wrong`, `superseded`, `operator` |
| Round kinds | `rebase` |
| Dependency check verdicts | `ok`, `missing`, `not-checked` |
| Phases | `running`, `stopped`, `reported`, `verifying`, `verdict_failed`, `awaiting_merge`, `merged`, `abandoned` |
| Verify kinds | `code`, `schema`, `design-doc` |
| Model tiers | `mechanical`, `implementation`, `judgement`, `verifier` |
| Notification events | `decision`, `abandon`, `push-failed`, `pr-closed`, `all-done`, `blocked`; also `workflow-pick` when listed in `notifications.events` |
| Adjacent change kinds (`[scope] adjacent`) | `lower-ratchet`, `stale-exemption`, `own-lint`, `own-dependents`, `own-registry`, `convention-place`, `moved-path` |

## Configuration

The project config is `.agentic-team.toml` in the repository root, in TOML. An optional, gitignored
`.agentic-team.local.toml` holds private or machine-specific values. It is merged into the tracked file table by
table; its keys win, and a list there replaces the tracked list. Omit a key to use its default. `""` or `[]` means the
item does not apply. The string `"TODO"` marks a value someone still has to fill in. Never put credentials or
secrets in either file.

Model values are either a model id (`"opus"`) or a table (`{ model = "sonnet", effort = "high" }`). A table may add
`profile`, a Claude profile for the sessions of that tier (see [Profiles](configuration.md#workers-on-more-than-one-claude-profile)). One optional table,
`[profiles]`, has names of your own and is not in the list below. So is the array of tables `[[workflow_rule]]`, the hard rules
of the workflows: each has a `name`, `match_paths` (globs over the write paths of a SCOPE) or `match_area` (the `area` meta),
and optionally `require_stage`, `approval` (a table of stage = level, for example `{ spec = "human" }`), `risk` (`low`,
`medium` or `high`, set on every stage task) and `on_timeout` (`approve` or `hold`; `hold` makes a `human` approval wait for the
owner with no deadline). See [Workflows](roles-and-briefs.md#workflows). How agents read the config, and what `check`
reports, is in [Configuration](configuration.md).

The config has 16 sections and 63 keys.

### `[taskgraph]`

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `project` | a string | `""` | Taskgraph project name (`tg projects` lists them). Required: `config.py check` fails while it is empty. |

### `[constraints]`

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `forbidden` | a list of strings | `[]` | One rule per item; they become FORBIDDEN in every brief. The template sets `["TODO"]` until someone confirms the list, even if it ends up empty. |

### `[autonomy]`

The grant never overrides safety rules, required approvals, or constraints. See the [decision-forks principle](../skills/principle-decision-forks/SKILL.md).

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `grant` | a string | `""` | Decisions and actions the Manager may take without asking. `""` means no standing grant. |
| `always_pause` | a list of strings | `[]` | Decisions that always need the operator, even under the grant. |

### `[sessions]`

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `max_parallel` | a positive integer | `2` | Cap on in-flight sessions, workers and verifiers. Start with 1 or 2. The Manager refills as sessions finish. |
| `permission_mode` | a non-empty string | `"auto"` | `--permission-mode` for worker sessions. |
| `timezone` | an IANA time zone name | the system time zone, else `UTC` | IANA zone name, for example `"Asia/Singapore"`. Used for the times that `status` shows and the TIMEZONE of the brief. `run.py` records its own times (`started_at`, `merged_at`, `Stopped:`) in UTC, ISO 8601, as `2026-11-17T09:05:00Z`; `status` reads an older local string (`2026-11-17 17:05 SGT`) too and shows it as it is. |
| `timezone_label` | a string | `""` | Label written after times, for example `"SGT"`. Set it when the derived label is an offset such as `+08`. |

### `[models]`

Any tier or override table may also set `profile = "<name>"` or `profile = ["<name>", ...]`. A string tier (`"opus"`) uses the Manager's own profile. See [Profiles](configuration.md#workers-on-more-than-one-claude-profile).

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mechanical` | a model id or { model = "...", effort = "...", profile = "..." } | `"haiku"` | Sweeps, counts, diffs, summaries. Use an alias: an older pinned id such as `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001` drops out of `auto` mode in a `--bg` worker and waits on a permission prompt. |
| `implementation` | a model id or { model = "...", effort = "...", profile = "..." } | `{ model = "sonnet", effort = "high" }` | Well-scoped build or edit work with a known answer shape. |
| `judgement` | a model id or { model = "...", effort = "...", profile = "..." } | `"opus"` | Judgement, review, prose readers rely on, long unattended runs. |
| `verifier` | a model id or { model = "...", effort = "...", profile = "..." } | unset | Verification sessions. Unset means a different model from the worker's: `opus`, or `sonnet` if the worker ran on `opus`. |
| `verifier_by_tier` | a table of tier or models.overrides key = model, for example { implementation = "sonnet" } | `{}` | `[models.verifier_by_tier]` maps a tier (`mechanical`, `implementation`, `judgement`) or a `[models.overrides]` key to the verifier model of a task on that tier: a model id or a table with `effort` and `profile`, as for a tier. See [Verifier model per tier](configuration.md#verifier-model-per-tier). Empty: `verifier` decides, as before. |
| `overrides` | a table of "work type" = model | `{}` | `[models.overrides]` maps a work type to a model, for example `"data migration" = { model = "opus", effort = "high" }`. Matched case-insensitively before the tiers. A task's `tier` meta may name an override key. |

### `[merge]`

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mode` | one of "local", "pr" | `"local"` | `local`: `close` merges into the main checkout under a `MERGE:` line, as before. `pr`: `close` pushes the task branch and opens a pull or merge request; `record` merges it under a `MERGE:` line when the host reports it clean, and records merges done by anyone from the request state. Setting `pr` is the operator's standing permission to push task branches and open requests. Merging still needs the `MERGE:` line. |
| `host` | one of "auto", "github", "gitlab" | `"auto"` | Which CLI speaks to the host: `gh` or `glab`. `auto` reads the `remote` URL: a host name of `github.com` means GitHub, a host name that contains `gitlab` means GitLab. A self-managed GitLab on another host name needs `host = "gitlab"`. Only read in `pr` mode. |
| `remote` | a non-empty string | `"origin"` | The git remote the host is reached through. |
| `base` | a string | `""` | The branch requests target. `""` means the host's default branch, asked once per `run.py` command. A task launched with `--base <branch>` targets that branch instead (meta `target`). |
| `method` | one of "merge", "squash", "rebase" | `"merge"` | How `record` merges. GitHub: `gh pr merge --merge\|--squash\|--rebase`. GitLab: the project's merge method setting decides between merge commit, rebase and fast-forward; `squash` adds `squash=true`, the other two values add nothing. |
| `catch_up` | one of "host", "local" | `"host"` | How `close` catches up a request that is behind its target, in `pr` mode. `host`: it asks the host to rebase the request (GitHub `gh pr update-branch --rebase`, GitLab `PUT merge_requests/<iid>/rebase`) and pushes nothing; a host that cannot rebase or refuses this user falls back to `local`. `local`: it rebases the branch in its idle worktree and pushes it under the lease. |
| `after_rebase` | a string | `""` | A shell command that checks the tree after every rebase that `run.py` does, takes from the host, or accepts from someone else, and on a rebase onto a newer target that `close` is about to push (the result of a rebase round or of a rebase by hand). Empty means no check. It runs in its own process group with a 10-minute timeout; an event keeps the last 5 lines of its output. A timeout, and a problem on this machine (a temporary worktree that cannot be made), are not a failure: nothing is accepted, pushed or started, a line says the check could not run, and the result is not kept. A pass or a failure is kept per (head, target, command) in `.agentic-team/after-rebase-cache.json`, so `record` runs the command once for each head. A non-zero exit counts as a conflict: `run.py round <id> rebase` starts a round when the merge of the head into the target passes `git merge-tree` but fails the check (the check runs in a temporary worktree of that merge); a local catch-up rebase (`catch_up = "local"`) runs it in the task worktree and, on a failure, puts the old head back and prints `conflict`; a rebase taken from the host or from someone else (#138) runs it in a temporary detached worktree of the new head under `.claude/worktrees/after-rebase-<id>`, which `run.py` always removes, and on a failure `pushed` stays and `conflict` is printed. Example: `after_rebase = 'test "$(alembic heads \| wc -l)" -eq 1'` fails a rebase that leaves two Alembic heads. |
| `draft` | true or false | `false` | `true` opens each request as a draft (GitHub `gh pr create --draft`, GitLab a `Draft: ` title), so it starts no full CI run until someone marks it ready; `record` reports `pr-draft` until it is. `false`: the request opens ready. |
| `remove_worktrees` | true or false | `true` | `true`: after a merge, `run.py` removes the task's worktrees and sessions when they are safe to remove (no session, process or container uses them, a clean tree whose ignored files are all disposable, a merged `HEAD`); see the cleanup in [Lifecycle](lifecycle.md#verdict-and-close). `false`: it removes nothing, and prints `kept <folder>: merge.remove_worktrees is false` once, at the merge. |
| `disposable` | a list of path patterns | `[]` | Ignored paths that `run.py` may delete with a merged worktree, added to the default list. An entry `"!<pattern>"` turns off one default pattern. See [Disposable patterns](configuration.md#disposable-patterns). |

### `[verify]`

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kind` | one of "code", "schema", "design-doc" | `"code"` | The verify kind of a task without a `verify_kind` meta. See [Task metadata](reference.md#task-metadata). |
| `revisions_per_attempt` | an integer that is 0 or more | `2` | The revisions (`run.py revise`) one attempt may have. `0` turns revisions off: the lifecycle of 0.23.0. The task's plan key `revisions` overrides it. See [Revisions](lifecycle.md#revisions-fix-in-place). |
| `keep_sessions_minutes` | a positive integer | `60` | How long the worker and the verifier stay idle after their newest row of the revision, waiting for a revision; then `record` stops them. |
| `seat` | one of "task", "own" | `"task"` | Where the verifier runs: `"task"`, the task worktree, read only, after the worker's turn; `"own"`, a `verify-<id>-<n>` folder, as before 0.24.0. |
| `seat_wait_minutes` | a positive integer | `5` | How long after a worker's report `verify` waits for a worker that is still busy (it refuses and names it) before the verifier gets a folder of its own. In a revision, a new verifier then replaces the kept one. |
| `ci_ref_prefix` | a branch name prefix that ends with - or / | `"ci-"` | The prefix of the scratch branch that `verify --ci-ref` pushes: `<prefix><id>-<attempt>`. ASCII letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `-` and `/`; no leading `-`, `.` or `/`, no `..` or `//`; it ends with `-` or `/`. Pick one that the push filter of your CI workflow matches. |

### `[roles]`

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `default` | a string | `""` | The role of a task with no `role` meta: `"architect"`, `"software-engineer"`, or a project role. `""` means no role. A name that has no role file makes `launch`, `adopt` and `verify` refuse. See [Roles](roles-and-briefs.md#roles). |

### `[workflow_policy]`

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | true or false | `false` | `true` turns workflows on: `config.py check` then validates the workflow files and the stage library, and a broken file is reported like a broken role file. `false` (the default) leaves workflows off. See [Workflows](roles-and-briefs.md#workflows). |
| `design_dir` | a string | `"docs/design"` | The folder of design documents: the `{design_dir}` in the scope template of a stage type of the stage library (`stages.toml`). A path relative to the repository root, without a trailing `/`. |
| `manager_due_hours` | a positive integer | `2` | Hours after a stage merges until the decision of its `manager` approval is due. At the due time `record` approves it by default. See [Workflows](roles-and-briefs.md#workflows). |
| `human_due_hours` | a positive integer | `48` | Hours after a stage merges until the decision of its `human` approval is due. At the due time `record` applies the default (approve), unless the rule that raised the approval sets `on_timeout = "hold"`. |
| `approval_floor` | a table of verify kind = "auto", "manager" or "human", for example { schema = "manager" } | `{}` | The lowest approval of a stage by its verify kind, for example `{ schema = "manager" }`: a stage whose verify kind is `schema` then needs at least a `manager` approval. The approval of a stage is the highest of its workflow value, the `approval` of a matching `[[workflow_rule]]` and this floor. |
| `when_unsure` | one of "lighter", "heavier", "figure-it-out" | `"lighter"` | What `add --pick` does when the two answers do not agree on one workflow. `"lighter"` (the default): two different names take the one with fewer required stages, a name with `unsure` takes the name, and two `unsure` take `figure-it-out`. `"heavier"`: two different names take the heavier one, and two `unsure` take the heaviest. `"figure-it-out"`: every row that has an `unsure` or a disagreement takes `figure-it-out`. The Manager never asks the owner; the choice is in the `workflow_record` and in the status report. See [Workflows](roles-and-briefs.md#workflows). |

### `[scope]`

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `adjacent` | a list of adjacent-change kinds | `[]` | Kinds of change outside a task's SCOPE that a worker may make without `BLOCKED`. `"lower-ratchet"`: only lower a baseline, ratchet or allow-list count (never raise it, never add an entry). `"stale-exemption"`: delete an exemption or baseline row that a scanner run in this attempt proves stale. `"own-lint"`: fix lint or format errors that this attempt's change caused in files outside SCOPE. `"own-dependents"`: change a caller, test, fixture, generated file, doc or API sample of the code that this attempt changes, as far as an ACCEPTANCE line, a VERIFY command or a gate that the brief names needs it. `"own-registry"`: add the entry that a check requires for a file this attempt adds, in a table that must list every file (never an exemption, a baseline row or an allow-list entry). `"convention-place"`: put new code in the file where the repository's conventions place it, for example a schema file or a facade, when that file is outside SCOPE. `"moved-path"`: change the code that a SCOPE path meant, when that path does not exist at the base and `git grep` finds that code in exactly one other place. When set, the worker brief's SCOPE gains one line that names the kinds, and the worker lists each such change under `Deviations:` as `adjacent: <kind>: <path>`. The verifier brief names the same kinds and checks each `adjacent:` line. |

### `[report]`

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `require_ran` | a table of verify kind = list of line prefixes, for example { "code" = ["reuse:"] } | `{}` | The line prefixes that a worker `PASS` report needs under `Ran:`, by verify kind (`code`, `schema`, `design-doc`): `require_ran = { "code" = ["reuse:", "mutation:"], "design-doc" = ["self-check:"] }`. The worker brief's `check-report` command carries one `--require-ran <prefix>` for each prefix of the task's verify kind, and refuses a `PASS` report that has no `Ran:` line starting with one of them, naming the missing prefixes. Empty: no check, as before. A key that is not a verify kind is a config error. |
| `checks` | a list of non-empty one-line shell commands | `[]` | Project commands that the worker's `check-report` runs before it accepts a `PASS`, for every verify kind. See [Report checks](operations.md#report-checks). |
| `checks_by_kind` | a table of verify kind = list of shell commands, for example { "design-doc" = ["python docs/check_refs.py"] } | `{}` | The same, for one verify kind (`code`, `schema`, `design-doc`); they run after `checks`: `[report.checks_by_kind]` `design-doc = ["python docs/models/check_refs.py"]`. A key that is not a verify kind is a config error. |
| `check_timeout_seconds` | a positive integer | `600` | The time that each check may take. A command must be one line: a command with a newline is a config error. |
| `summary_lang` | one of "en", "zh" | `"en"` | The language that the worker and the verifier write their `Summary:` line in (the brief says so in English). Project code and every runtime file stay English. See [Issue comment summaries](github-backend.md#issue-comment-summaries). |

### `[messaging]`

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `asks_per_attempt` | an integer that is 0 or more | `3` | How many asks a worker may file in one attempt. `0` forbids asks. A task's `asks` meta overrides it; the `mechanical` tier defaults to `0`. |
| `ask_due_minutes` | a positive integer | `60` | An ask with no answer after this long prints `ask-due` at each `record`, with the hint `run.py answer <id> --default`. |
| `pending_minutes` | a positive integer | `10` | A message that was posted to a socket and has no ack after this long goes back to pending, and the next delivery resumes the session. A message that a busy worker has not seen after this long prints `steer-pending`. |
| `doorbell` | one of "socket", "resume" | `"socket"` | `"socket"`: post the doorbell to the worker's inbox socket, and fall back to stop plus resume. `"resume"`: always stop plus resume. `config.py check` warns when it is `"socket"` and a settings file puts the Manager in `bypassPermissions`. |
| `tg_poll_seconds` | a positive integer | `5` | The default of `run.py wait --tg-interval`. |

### `[brief]`

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `carried_report_bytes` | a positive integer | `3000` | The most UTF-8 bytes of one carried report (the previous attempt, an upstream dependency, the worker report in a verify brief) in a brief. A report over it is cut at a line boundary and ends with a line that names its result id and the command that prints it. |
| `carried_total_bytes` | a positive integer | `12000` | The most UTF-8 bytes of all carried reports of one brief together. It must be at least `carried_report_bytes`. |

### `[notifications]`

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `skill` | a string | `""` | Skill for operator messages, for example `"telegram-send:telegram-send"`. With `""`, the Manager reports only in the conversation. |
| `events` | a list of notification events: "decision", "abandon", "push-failed", "pr-closed", "all-done", "blocked", "workflow-pick" | `["decision", "abandon", "push-failed", "pr-closed", "all-done", "blocked"]` | The events that queue a notice (see [Notifications](operations.md#notifications)). `[]` queues none. |
| `digest` | one of "off", "daily" | `"off"` | `"daily"`: `run.py notify-queue --digest` prints one digest a day: merged, in flight, decisions waiting. |

### `[hooks]`

Worker hooks (see [Worker hooks](operations.md#worker-hooks)). All off until `enabled` is `true`.

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | true or false | `false` | The master switch. With `false`, nothing here has an effect and the launch line is as in 0.28.2. |
| `layered` | true or false | `true` | When enabled: reduce the output of the commands in `commands`. |
| `compact_pins` | true or false | `true` | When enabled: keep the task's essentials through a compaction. |
| `summarize_fallback` | true or false | `false` | When enabled: when a failed command's output is above `large_chars` and no extraction rule matched, ask Haiku (`claude -p --model haiku`) for a summary. It takes 7 to 12 seconds a call and uses the subscription. |
| `passthrough_chars` | a positive integer | `20000` | Output below this size is left unchanged. |
| `large_chars` | a positive integer | `100000` | The Haiku fallback runs only above this size. At least `passthrough_chars`. |
| `summarize_seconds` | a positive integer | `30` | The Haiku fallback gives up after this long; the session then sees the last lines and the path of the full output. |
| `commands` | a list of command prefixes or globs, none empty | `["make test*", "pytest", "python* -m pytest*", "uv run pytest", "vitest", "npx vitest", "pnpm test*", "playwright", "npx playwright", "gh run view --log", "docker logs"]` | The commands whose output is reduced. A string with `*`, `?` or `[` is a glob over the whole command (`make test*` matches `make test-unit FOO=1`). Any other string is a prefix: its words that do not start with `-` must begin the command, and each word after the last such word that starts with `-` must be one of the command's words (`gh run view --log` matches `gh run view 123 --log`; a `-` word before the last plain word belongs to the prefix, so `python -m pytest` is a prefix; `pytest` matches `pytest -x tests/` and not `cat pytest.ini`). A setting replaces the list; it does not add to it. |

### `[rounds]`

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cap` | a positive integer | `3` | The rounds (`run.py round`) a task may have without `--attempt`. A round does not count toward the attempt cap. At the cap a `conflict` line names the decision and the override. |
| `verify` | one of "always", "by-risk" | `"always"` | `"always"`: a round's PASS goes to a verifier session, whatever the task's risk and verify kind, unless its head carries the same change as the verified head. `"by-risk"`: the rule of a plain attempt (a verifier for `risk=high`, CI verify, or a kind that is not `code`). |

## Task metadata

Task notes hold the purpose and acceptance criteria, following the Taskgraph skill. Metadata holds everything else. There are 62 keys.

| Key | Set by | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `scope`, `verify`, `tier`, `risk` | plan | Brief inputs. `tier` is a tier name or a `models.overrides` key. `risk=high` sends verification to a separate session. |
| `role` | plan | The task's role: a name from `run.py roles`. Empty or absent means the config's `roles.default`, else no role. See [Roles](roles-and-briefs.md#roles). |
| `estimate` | plan | Taskgraph's own estimate in hours. The worker's timebox is twice it. |
| `workflow`, `workflow_record` | `add --workflow` | On a workflow instance task: the workflow's name, and its record as JSON (`workflow`, `version`, `optional`, `rule`, `pick`: the two answers, their seeds, the workflow resolved, the resolution rule and whether it was unsure; `rules`: each hard rule that matched, with what it did; `picked_at`, `overrides`, `adjustments`, `ended`, `scope`, `verify`, and `stages`: each stage's `id`, `type`, `task`, `approval`, `approval_id`, `split`, `after` and `parts`). The instance is never launched; its status is the derived status of its stages. |
| `stage`, `stage_part`, `stage_origin`, `split_declined`, `workflow_notes` | `add --workflow`, `stage split`, `stage approve` | On a stage task: its stage id; the part number of a split stage; how it came to exist (`expand`, `with` or `split`); the one line that declined a split; and the workflow's notes for the stage, which the brief pastes under CONTEXT. |
| `approval_id` | `add --workflow` | On a stage task that has an approval: the id of its decision. |
| `approval_for`, `approval_stage`, `approval_level`, `approval_state`, `on_timeout`, `due_at`, `decide_by`, `default` | `add --workflow`, the merge record, `record`, `stage approve` | On an approval decision: the stage task and stage id it answers, its level (`manager` or `human`), its state (`pending` until the stage merges, `open`, `done`), what happens at the due time (`on_timeout`: `approve` or `hold`), the due time (`due_at`, UTC; `decide_by` is its date for Taskgraph) and the `default` that `record` applies. A `human` decision has `decider=manager` until the stage merges, then `operator`. |
| `verify_mode` | plan | `session` (the default) or `ci:<name>`. `ci:<name>`: the CI run on the pushed head is the verifier. GitHub: `<name>` is a workflow file name or workflow name. GitLab: `pipeline` for the whole pipeline, or a job name. |
| `verify_kind` | plan | `code` (default), `schema` or `design-doc`. Selects the verifier's method text and the pass level: `code` closes on `artifact-verified` or `test-verified`; the other two only on `artifact-verified`. Unset means the config's `verify.kind`. |
| `started_at`, `session`, `model`, `attempt` | `launch`, `adopt` | The current attempt, and when it started (UTC, ISO 8601; a task from 0.27.2 or older has a local string). `adopt` writes `session=adopted` and no `model`. |
| `sessions` | `launch`, `verify`, `adopt` | A JSON list with one entry per session `run.py` started: `{"id", "kind" (task or verify), "attempt", "name", "worktree"}` (a verifier in the task worktree has `"worktree": "task-<id>"` and its own name `verify-<id>-<n>`; its identity is that name, not the folder), `"profile"` for a session that runs under a profile other than the Manager's own, and `"sessionId"` (the full id that `--resume` needs) when the `claude agents` row had one. Every entry that `run.py` starts also has `"plugin"`, the agentic-team version of the `run.py` that started it (from `plugin.json`), and a worker's entry from `launch` has `"cause"`: why the attempt started, one of `first`, `review-fix` (a verifier's `verify-failed` verdict on a PASS), `ci-fix` (the same from a CI run), `rebase` (a `round`), `retry-issues` (the worker reported `ISSUES` or `BLOCKED`), `retry-stopped`, `retry-died`. `launch` derives it from the rows of the attempt before it, and leaves it out, with a note in the `launched` line, when they do not say (a stuck session, an abandon for another reason); `launch --cause <cause>` sets it. `record` adds `"usage"` (`{"out", "in", "cache_read", "cache_write"}`: the tokens summed over the session's transcript without the messages of the sessions it resumed, and `"partial": true` when a session of its chain was lost) once the session is no longer live and its transcript is found; an entry whose transcript cannot be read is tried again by the next `record`. `id` is the short id that `claude --bg` printed, checked against `claude agents`. `launch` and `adopt` add `"role"`, `"tier"` and `"verify_kind"` (see [Roles](roles-and-briefs.md#roles)); an adopted attempt has an entry with these and no `"id"`. A revision's resume adds an entry with the new id, the same name, `"resumed_from"` (the old id) and `"revision"`.
